rules_evaluated.evidence: The one forcing function with no fence is the diff push-back (## Read the diff and push back on a line, L24-27): no {{prompt:}} block, pure body prose. Harm the rule guards against: a speed-runner who reads fences only would skip a scripted-count nicety, but here skipping the beat skips the exercise's stated point (L9: "pushing back is core work") — exactly the collapse the rule's own removal test flags. But this exact question is a documented maintainer accept-note, not an oversight: maintainer block L53 ("Carded and kept... the compound-step mention in the push-back bullet stays") and backing Stance L94-97 ("the student writes their own push-back with no prompt supplied, which is slower and worse-scaffolded on purpose, because the words have to be theirs when the compound step reuses them") state the design reason directly — a fence would hand the student a template instead of forcing their own wording, defeating the forcing function's actual purpose. Trace confirms it lands in-room (mood 8/8) with the trainer narrating the beat live.
